findings.message: This fixes only one case of the problem. Only `form.confirm.label` now reads Through from the field. `title` and `look.confirm` still use `suffix`, which is built once from the drafted `a.through`. The e2e locates the confirm group by that label ("Confirm: Add Dinesh Wickrama to TMT, Mar–May"). `look.done` also still uses `when` and `a.percent` from the draft, even though Percent and Through can both be edited on the card. After an edit, the card's group name and its "Added …" line describe a range and percent that were never written. The previous finding named the title, `look.confirm`, the `done` line and the button. Only the button was fixed. Fix: build the title, `look.confirm` and `done` from the confirmed values as well, with `{through}` and `{percent}` templates, or rebuild them on edit.
findings.scenario: Card drafted for Mar–May at 50%. The person sets Through to 2027-04 and Percent to 30, then confirms. The button says Mar–Apr, but the card's group label still says Mar–May and the done line reads "Added Dinesh Wickrama to TMT · 50% Mar–May". The rows written are Mar–Apr at 30%.

findings.message: An entity with no time zone still silently falls back to UTC. The only flag is a note on the chat card (`zoneNote` via `linkNote`). `addPerson` over MCP (agents are the main channel), `recordLeaver` and `applyStatusDates` all still decide joining, active and left by UTC, and nothing tells the caller. The service's result and audit don't record that UTC was used. The previous finding asked addPerson to refuse or flag this, and to test the Australian entity without the planted zone. The new test checks only the note string, never the date that gets saved. Fix: make `entityToday` fail closed when `entityZoneSet` returns null, or have addPerson and recordLeaver refuse until the zone is set (or return a flag and record it). Add a test that runs addPerson for the Australian entity with no zone set.
findings.scenario: An agent calls add_person over MCP for Lumen Labs Pty Ltd (no entity_zone row) at 2026-11-15T20:00Z, which is the 16th in Sydney. joined_on is saved as 2026-11-15, with no note and nothing in the result or audit.

findings.message: The job now uses each entity's own today, but it still runs once a day at 00:05 UTC (`cron: "5 0 * * *"`). Eastern entities have their dates applied hours late, and an entity west of UTC a whole day late. Meanwhile `addPerson` and `recordLeaver` decide by the same local today straight away, so 'one today' still disagrees across the day. Fix: run the job hourly so each entity moves soon after its own midnight. The service is idempotent, so re-running it is safe.
findings.scenario: A Sydney person has joined_on 2026-11-16. Their day starts at 2026-11-15T13:00Z, but the job runs at 2026-11-16T00:05Z, so they stay 'joining' until 11:05 Sydney time and are left out of `listPeople({status:['active']})` picks. For an entity in America/New_York, the 00:05Z run on the 16th sees the local 15th, so the person stays 'joining' for all of 16 Nov.

findings.message: The fix sends two callers through `endSlot`: `extendStanding` and `endStandingForLeaver`. The test checks only the job's audit `before.ended[0].rows`. Nothing checks the leaver handler's audit or events, or the allocationSet event either path now sends. Without the fix, a regression in the leaver path or in the event would stay green. Fix: write a table-driven test over the job end and the leaver end, driven through the real path (recordLeaver → personLeft handler). Assert the audit's removed rows and standing rows, and that the event has months [], percent 0 and standing true.
findings.scenario: Revert only `endStandingForLeaver` to the old loop that drops what setStanding returns. Every test still passes, even though the leaver's removed months are missing from the audit again.

findings.message: zoneNote catches every entityOf error with `.catch(() => null)`. An ambiguous entity, an unknown entity and a failed query all come back as `undefined`, the same value the function gives for 'this entity has a zone'. So a lookup that could not run reads as 'no warning needed'. Fix: let query failures propagate, or return a distinct 'could not check the zone' note. Only an entity that was resolved and has a zone should give no note.
findings.scenario: A transient DB error, or an entity 'AU' matching two Australian entities, makes entityOf throw. zoneNote returns undefined, and the card shows no UTC warning even if neither entity has a zone.

findings.message: `monthShort` is a second copy of the allocations `monthLabel` short format, and the button label now joins the two: the start month from server-side `monthLabel` and the end month from client-side `monthShort`. They agree today, but one can change without the other. Consider one shared month formatter.

The missing-zone case is flagged only in the chat card's note (zoneNote through linkNote). addPerson itself, recordLeaver and applyStatusDates still fall back to UTC through entityZone without a word. Over MCP or any other non-card caller there is no flag at all: the result, the audit and the event all carry a UTC-derived date as if it were the entity's local today. Even with the note showing, confirm still saves the UTC date. Fix: have addPerson, and every HR status decision that goes through entityToday, refuse when entityZoneSet is null (or put an explicit flag in the result and audit), instead of only advising on the card.
findings.scenario: Over MCP: add_person { entity: 'Australia' } at 2026-11-15T20:00Z, with no workflows.entity_zone row and AU missing from ENTITY_ZONES. joined_on is saved as 2026-11-15, though it is already 2026-11-16 in Sydney, and the response and audit don't flag that UTC was used.

findings.message: HR still has a second 'today' rule. changePersonRun defaults `effectiveOn` to UTC `today()` and requires `on === today()` for person-level fields. The same goes for `personByNo` (records.ts:36, `employmentAt(today())`) and the contract readers. Meanwhile addPerson, recordLeaver and the status job now decide by the entity's local today. Near midnight the two rules disagree about the same person at the same moment. Fix: send HR's default effective dates and in-force reads through entityToday for the person's entity.
findings.scenario: At 2026-11-15T20:00Z, add a Sri Lanka person: joined_on is 2026-11-16 and status is active. Changing their title right after without effectiveOn writes an employment period effective 2026-11-15, the day before they joined. And personByNo's employmentAt(2026-11-15) finds no employment in force for them.
